output.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just a finance problem
output.body:
Late payment terms usually show up as a workflow problem before they show up as a finance problem. For a small business owner, the real question is not whether the terms are bad, but which repeating task is creating the drag: invoice tracking, chasing overdue payments, or an aging report in a spreadsheet. That is the bounded decision worth making first.

The useful test is simple: is the work repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time? If yes, it may be a fit for AI or workflow automation. If it changes a lot from case to case, or if it touches money movement, keep human approval in place and leave the high-risk step manual. That is policy, not a promise, and the diagnostic should say plainly when AI is not the right tool.

Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP if the workflow fits. Those timings are intended scopes, not guarantees.

A practical next step: take the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up the same every time? If yes, you have a workflow to examine. If no, you have a judgment call that stays with you. Dry, but useful.
